types.name: Ratios from one given ratio
types.description: One ratio (such as tan θ = 2/3) or two sides of a right triangle are given and the question asks for another ratio, a side, or an expression built from sin, cos and tan of that angle.

types.name: Standard angle values
types.description: The expression uses only fixed angles like 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° or 90° and asks for its value, or asks for angles A and B from equations such as tan(A + B) = √3.

types.name: Simplifying identities
types.description: An expression in θ with no extra condition must be simplified, proved, or matched to an option, often written as "is equal to" or "find k" where k is another trig ratio.

types.name: Given a condition, find a value
types.description: A relation between ratios of θ is given (such as sec θ + tan θ = p, sin θ + cos θ = p, or an equation in θ) and the question asks for the value of another expression.

types.name: Complementary angles
types.description: Angles that add up to 90° appear (such as 25° and 65°, or sin A = cos B), including long sums or products like sin²1° + … + sin²89° or tan 1° tan 2° … tan 89°.

types.name: Compound and double angles
types.description: The question uses sin, cos or tan of a sum, difference, double or triple angle, or values like sin 15°, tan 75° or sin 18°.

types.name: Angles beyond 90° and radians
types.description: The angle is negative, greater than 90°, or given in radians (such as cos 120°, tan(−1125°) or cos(17π/3)), so it must be reduced using signs in the four quadrants.

types.name: Maximum and minimum values
types.description: The question asks for the greatest or least value of a trigonometric expression, such as a sin θ + b cos θ or 25 cos²x + 9 sec²x.

types.name: Heights and distances
types.description: A word problem about towers, buildings, poles, ships, kites or shadows with angles of elevation or depression.
